title: Change and compare
goal: I can use bar models for before and after. I ask what stays the same: the total, the difference or one amount.

learn.intro: Draw a model for the Before and a model for the After. Ask first: what stays the same?

example.problem: Kumar has 60 cards. Wei has 30 cards. Kumar gives some cards to Wei. Then Kumar has 2/3 as many cards as Wei. How many cards does Kumar give?
steps: Kumar gives cards to Wei, so the total stays the same: 60 + 30 = 90.
After: Kumar has 2 units and Wei has 3 units. That is 5 units in all.
5 units = 90, so 1 unit = 18. Kumar now has 2 × 18 = 36.

howto.title: How to
steps: Draw the Before bars. Draw the After bars.
Ask what stays the same. Make that part match.
Find 1 unit. Then answer the question.

facts.title: What stays the same?
lines: A gives to B: the total.
Both get or lose the same: the difference.
Only one thing changes: the other amount.

try.text: Jason has 70 stickers. Amelia has 50 stickers. Jason gives some stickers to Amelia. Then Jason has 3/5 as many stickers as Amelia. How many stickers does Jason give? {b}
try.explanation: The total stays the same: 70 + 50 = 120. After, Jason has 3 units and Amelia has 5 units. 8 units = 120, so 1 unit = 15. Jason now has 3 × 15 = 45. Jason gives 70 - 45 = 25 stickers.

items.text: Aisha has $80. A book takes 1/4 of her money. A pen takes 1/3 of the money that is then left.
Lily has 22 counters. Ravi has 14 counters. Lily gives 5 counters to Ravi.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The total is {b} before and after.

items.explanation: (a) 22 - 5 = 17. (b) 14 + 5 = 19. (c) 22 + 14 = 36, and 17 + 19 = 36. Giving does not change the total.

items.text: Ben is 12 years old. His aunt is 41 years old.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In 6 years Ben will be {b} and his aunt will be {b}.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Now the aunt is {b} years older than Ben. In 6 years she is {b} years older.

items.explanation: (a) 12 + 6 = 18 and 41 + 6 = 47. (b) 41 - 12 = 29 and 47 - 18 = 29. When both get older by the same number of years, the difference stays the same.

items.text: Ali has 38 stamps. Mei has 24 stamps. Ali gives some stamps to Mei. Then each child has an equal number of stamps. How many stamps does Ali give? {b}
items.explanation: The total stays 38 + 24 = 62. Each has 62 ÷ 2 = 31. Ali has 38 - 31 = 7 stamps too many, so he gives 7.

items.text: There are 48 children. 5/12 of them wear glasses. How many more children do not wear glasses than wear glasses? {b}
items.explanation: 1/12 of 48 = 4. 5/12 of 48 = 20 wear glasses. 48 - 20 = 28 do not. 28 - 20 = 8 more.

items.text: A bag has 15 green beads and 9 yellow beads. Then 6 more yellow beads are put in.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The beads that did not change are   {circ:green|yellow}

parts.label: b
parts.text: At first, green beads are {b} of the beads.  (simplest form)

parts.label: c
parts.text: Now, green beads are {b} of the beads.  (simplest form)

items.explanation: (a) Only yellow beads were added, so the 15 green beads did not change. (b) At first there are 24 beads: 15/24 = 5/8. (c) Now there are 30 beads: 15/30 = 1/2. The green beads stay the same but they are a smaller part of the bag.

items.text: Ray spent 2/5 of his money on a bag. He has $45 left. Use the bar model.
items.explanation: The bag takes 2 of the 5 parts. The other 3 parts are $45, so 1 part = 45 ÷ 3 = 15. All 5 parts = 5 × 15 = 75.

items.text: A pen costs 1/3 as much as a book. The pen and the book cost $28 together.
items.explanation: The book is 3 units and the pen is 1 unit. 4 units = 28, so 1 unit = 7. The pen costs 7. The book costs 3 × 7 = 21.

items.text: Mei has 3/4 as many stickers as Siti. They have 56 stickers altogether.
items.explanation: Siti has 4 units and Mei has 3 units. 7 units = 56, so 1 unit = 8. Siti has 4 × 8 = 32. Mei has 3 × 8 = 24.

items.text: What stays the same? Circle one choice for each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Ali gives some marbles to Ben.   {circ:the total|the difference}

parts.label: b
parts.text: Ravi and Ali are each given $5.   {circ:the total|the difference}

parts.label: c
parts.text: Red beads are added to a jar of red and blue beads.   {circ:the red beads|the blue beads}

items.explanation: (a) Ben gains what Ali loses, so the total is the same. (b) Both gain $5, so the gap between them is the same, but the total goes up by $10. (c) Only red beads are put in, so the number of blue beads does not change.

items.text: Ravi has $45. Ben has $21. Their mother gives each boy $15.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Ravi has $ {b} more than Ben now.

items.explanation: (a) 45 + 15 = 60. (b) 21 + 15 = 36. (c) 60 - 36 = 24. Before the gift 45 - 21 = 24 too. The difference did not change.

items.text: Siti buys a shirt with 1/4 of her money. Shoes take 1/3 of the rest. She keeps $30. How much money did Siti start with? $ {b}
items.explanation: The shirt is 1 unit and the rest is 3 units. The shoes are 1/3 of the rest, which is 1 unit. So 4 - 1 - 1 = 2 units are left. 2 units = $30, so 1 unit = $15. At first she had 4 × 15 = $60.

items.text: A jug was 5/6 full of juice. After 250 ml was poured out, it was 1/2 full. How much juice does the jug hold when it is full? {b} ml
items.explanation: 5/6 - 1/2 = 5/6 - 3/6 = 2/6 = 1/3 of the jug was poured out. 1/3 is 250 ml, so a full jug is 3 × 250 = 750 ml.

items.text: Circle True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.text: When Ali gives Ben some stickers, the total number of stickers changes.   {circ:True|False}

parts.label: b
parts.text: When 2 children are each given $5, the difference between their money stays the same.   {circ:True|False}

parts.label: c
parts.text: If Mei has 1/2 as many cards as Ali, then Ali has 2 times as many cards as Mei.   {circ:True|False}

items.explanation: (a) False: what Ali loses Ben gains. (b) True: both amounts go up by 5. (c) True: if Mei has 1 unit, Ali has 2 units.

items.text: On Monday Siti uses 2/5 of her money. On Tuesday she uses 1/3 of what is left. In all she uses $90. How much money did Siti start with? $ {b}
items.hint: Cut the whole into 15 equal units. Count the units spent.
items.explanation: 2/5 = 6/15, so Monday takes 6 of 15 units. The rest is 9 units. Tuesday is 1/3 of 9 = 3 units. In all 6 + 3 = 9 units are spent. 9 units = $90, so 1 unit = $10. At first Siti had 15 × 10 = $150.

items.text: Siti and Mei have 120 beads altogether. Siti gives 10 beads to Mei. Then Siti has 3/5 as many beads as Mei. How many beads did Siti have at first? {b}
items.hint: The total stays the same. Find each child's beads after.
items.explanation: After: Siti 3 units, Mei 5 units. 8 units = 120, so 1 unit = 15. Siti has 45 now. She gave away 10, so at first she had 45 + 10 = 55.

items.text: Ravi is 38 years old. His son is 10 years old. In how many years will the son be 1/3 of his father's age? {b} years
items.hint: The difference in their ages never changes. How many units is it?
items.explanation: The difference is 38 - 10 = 28 years, and it stays 28. When the son is 1 unit the father is 3 units, so the difference is 2 units. 2 units = 28, so 1 unit = 14. The son is 14, which is 4 years from now.

items.text: Ali, Ben and Cara have 150 stickers altogether. Ali has twice as many stickers as Ben. Ben has 10 more than Cara.
items.hint: Call Cara's stickers 1 unit. Draw bars for Ben and for Ali.
items.explanation: Let Cara have 1 unit. Ben has 1 unit + 10. Ali has twice Ben: 2 units + 20. Altogether: 4 units + 30 = 150. So 4 units = 120 and 1 unit = 30. Cara 30, Ben 40, Ali 80.

items.text: In a hall, 2/5 of the people are children. Then 15 adults leave and 15 children come in. Now 1/2 of the people are children. How many people are in the hall? {b}
items.hint: The total stays the same. How much more of the total is children?
items.explanation: The number of people stays the same. At first children are 2/5 of the total. Now they are 1/2. 1/2 - 2/5 = 1/10 of the total is 15 children. So the total is 10 × 15 = 150.

items.text: A jar holds red beads and white beads. Red beads make up 2/7 of the jar. Then 24 red beads are taken out. Now red beads make up 1/6 of the jar. How many beads were in the jar at first? {b}
items.hint: The white beads do not change. What fraction of each total is white?
items.explanation: The white beads did not change. At first white is 5/7 of the beads. Now white is 5/6 of the beads. Let the white beads be 5 parts: at first the total is 7 parts, now it is 6 parts. 1 part = 24 beads, because 24 red beads were taken out. At first 7 × 24 = 168 beads.

items.text: Ali and Ben have 120 marbles altogether. Ali gives 1/3 of his marbles to Ben. Then Ben has 3 times as many marbles as Ali. How many marbles did Ali have at first? {b}
items.hint: After giving, Ali has 2/3 of his marbles. Ben has 3 times that.
items.explanation: Let Ali have 3 units at first. He gives 1 unit and keeps 2 units. Now Ben has 3 times as many: 6 units. After, the total is 2 + 6 = 8 units = 120, so 1 unit = 15. Ali had 3 × 15 = 45. Ben had 6 units - 1 unit = 5 units = 75 at first.

items.text: Jenny pays 1/5 of her money for a book. A bag takes 1/2 of the rest. She keeps $24. How much money did Jenny start with? $ {b}
items.explanation: The book is 1 unit and the rest is 4 units. The bag is 1/2 of 4 = 2 units. 5 - 1 - 2 = 2 units are left. 2 units = $24, so 1 unit = $12. At first Jenny had 5 × 12 = $60.

items.text: Jamie has 46 cards. Jason has 30 cards. Jamie gives some cards to Jason. Then they have equal numbers. How many cards does Jamie give? {b}
items.explanation: The total is 76, so each has 38. Jamie has 46 - 38 = 8 too many. Jamie gives 8 cards.

items.text: Amelia has $50. Ray has $30. They are each given the same amount. Then Ray has 3/4 as much as Amelia. How much is each given? $ {b}
items.explanation: The difference stays $20. After the gift Ray has 3 units and Amelia has 4 units, so the difference is 1 unit. 1 unit = $20. Amelia has $80 now, so the gift is 80 - 50 = $30.

items.text: A jar has 18 blue beads and 12 yellow beads. Then 20 yellow beads are put in.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The beads that did not change are   {circ:blue|yellow}

parts.label: b
parts.text: The fraction of beads that are blue is now {b}

items.explanation: (a) Only yellow beads were added, so the 18 blue beads did not change. (b) Now there are 18 + 32 = 50 beads. 18/50 = 9/25.
